decision_reason: The public repository is a USGS/CDI slide-deck workspace, not a standalone software product. Its README describes creating Reveal.js slides with Quarto; the source consists of a conference talk QMD and PowerPoint template, with no independent service, reusable product release, or documented software reuse. The primary-evidence/notability check therefore fails even though provenance, access, and CC0 are clear.

decision_reason: This is the source project for the named USGS Oahu Tsunami Evacuation Dashboard, an official public-facing interactive tool developed with the Hawaiʻi Emergency Management Agency for Oʻahu emergency managers and the public. The repository includes the Tableau workbook used to create the dashboard and the HTML source that embeds the same named Tableau Public view; the official USGS tool page still links to the live deployment. Repository CC0 covers the project work, and bundled Adobe Spry menu scripts retain their own BSD-style notices.

government_provenance.note: The official USGS CDI project page identifies the exact Oʻahu dashboard, USGS Western Geographic Science Center team, design consultation with the Oʻahu emergency manager, and USGS dashboard delivery.

public_source.note: The public USGS GitLab repository exposes the Dashboard_10_11.twbx Tableau workbook and the HTML embedding source without credentials; the HTML and workbook identify the same Dashboard_10_11 view linked from the official USGS page.

eligible_license.note: The project dedicates its own work worldwide under CC0-1.0. Bundled Adobe Spry scripts identify their own BSD-style source/binary redistribution terms in file headers (for example https://code.usgs.gov/cdi/projects/cdi-fy16/evac_dash/-/raw/master/SpryAssets/SpryWidget.js); these separate terms do not negate the eligible project grant.

primary_evidence.note: The exact named USGS tool page describes the public evacuation dashboard and links the live web tool; the USGS CDI project page documents its purpose and delivery to Oʻahu emergency managers and the public.

status_note: The surviving GitLab history first shows LICENSE.md in a 2018-02-28 commit; the official 2017 USGS CDI page links the dashboard and its former Bitbucket code repository, but an earlier licensed-source year could not be established. decision_reason: The FY17 USGS report documents this script as one component of a historical photo-publishing toolkit and gives it a useful Adobe Bridge installation guide, but the assigned repository is not the separate web-map application and has no versioned release, current product-specific use/support, or demonstrated independent reuse. The repository is explicitly archival, and the primary-evidence/notability baseline is not met. In addition, the source file attributes underlying DIYMetadata code to Paul Riggott while the repo offers CC0 without an upstream grant for that original code; its eligible-license scope remains unresolved. The primary-evidence failure is independently decisive for rejection.

government_provenance.note: The official FY17 CDI funded-project report identifies Sarah Nagorsen (USGS) as PI, describes the photo-publishing toolkit, and links this exact photometadata repository as its Adobe Bridge EXIF script.

public_source.note: The public USGS GitLab project exposes the GeotagPhotoMetadata.jsx script and CSV template without credentials.

eligible_license.note: Root LICENSE.md claims a worldwide CC0 dedication for the project, but the actual script header says DIYMetadata was written by Paul Riggott and modified/renamed by USGS author Sarah Nagorsen. No grant covering Riggott's original code was located, so CC0 scope for this material derivative cannot be verified.

primary_evidence.note: The report supports historical inclusion of the script in one Grand Canyon photo collection workflow, not a current standalone product or independent reuse. The assigned repository is marked Archival, has no tags/versioned release, and is distinct from the separate JavaScript/Python web-map application; no current-use/support signal or notability pathway for this exact script repo was found.

agency: U.S. Geological Survey, Community for Data Integration FY17 project; principal investigator Sarah Nagorsen (USGS)

status_note: The script identifies Riggott as the original DIYMetadata author and dates Nagorsen's modification to 2017-08-15; the file appears in the public project tree by 2017-10-16. The project-wide LICENSE.md was added 2020-03-23, which is not a defensible first open-source year while the upstream license scope remains unclear. README documentation requires Adobe Bridge CS6 or CC; code.json now marks this project Archival, and its 2024 metadataLastUpdated field is not a source change.
